etymologies.etymologyHTML: From ethic +‎ -al, from Late Latin ethicus (“moral, ethical”), from Ancient Greek ἠθικός (ēthikós, “of or for morals, moral, expressing character”), from ἦθος (êthos, “character, moral nature”).

definitions.definition: (philosophy, not comparable) Of or relating to the study of ethics.
(not comparable) Of or relating to the accepted principles of right and wrong, especially those of some organization or profession.
(of a drug, not comparable) Only dispensed on the prescription of a physician.
An ethical drug, one only dispensed on the prescription of a physician.
